messages:
elaine-contoso: Hey team — our Private control plane connection from Contoso's VPC started failing this morning. We see mTLS handshake errors in our app logs when trying to reach control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal:443. Error: TLSv1.3 alert internal_error / certificate_verify_failed. Can you advise?

ashley (support): Thanks Elaine. Can you paste the client-side openssl logs and the first TLS error from the control plane? Also, do you have any TLS inspection / proxy in front of outbound connections?

elaine-contoso: Pasting the client capture (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-18 09:12:34] openssl s_client -connect control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal:443 -cert user.crt -key user.key -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
write:errno=104
139847...: SSL routines:tls_construct_server_hello:no shared cipher:SSL alert number 40
```
Our network team says they haven't changed firewall rules. No explicit proxy configured, but we do have a corporate TLS inspection appliance that intercepts egress.

samir (netops): Reproduced similar symptom last quarter — TLS inspection appliances often strip or rewrite SNI or fail on client cert forwarding, causing cert_verify failures. Two quick checks: 1) confirm SNI in flight, 2) check whether the appliance terminates TLS and re-creates a new TLS session to upstream (breaking mTLS).

jin (eng-infra): +1. Redwood Private control plane requires end-to-end mTLS with the customer client cert presented to our control plane (we validate client cert chain). If a middlebox terminates TLS and re-initiates to us, the client cert won't be forwarded and the handshake fails.

ashley (support): Can you try a packet capture showing TLS ClientHello to the external IP (before and after the appliance)? If customer's appliance does MITM, you'll see two separate TLS handshakes: client -> appliance and appliance -> control-plane. Also confirm SNI header present in ClientHello (we expect control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal).

elaine-contoso: I grabbed a tcpdump from the border router. ClientHello shows SNI set to control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal, but when our appliance forwards the connection, the SNI in the outgoing ClientHello is replaced with control-plane.redwood.internal (no contoso subdomain). That could be the issue?

samir (netops): Yep — SNI rewrite + termination will break the client cert flow. On some appliances you can enable "passthrough" or an allowlist to skip inspection for specific FQDNs. Ask security to add control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal to the TLS-inspection bypass.

jin (eng-infra): Also check ciphers and TLS version. While we support TLS1.2/1.3, some middleboxes downgrade connections. Run this from an internal host that bypasses the appliance if possible:
```
openssl s_client -connect 34.198.12.145:443 -servername control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal -cert ./client.crt -key ./client.key -msg
```
If that succeeds and the appliance path fails, it's definitely the appliance.

ashley (support): Incident bot created ticket RW-INC-2026-418 and escalated to eng-infra. @jin can you validate whether we can accept connections where SNI is rewritten (short answer: we require client cert CN to match allowed principals and SNI mismatch will fail authorization).

jin (eng-infra): We do policy checks that include SNI and client cert metadata. If SNI != expected host, the connection is rejected. We cannot accept rewritten SNI because it undermines tenant isolation.

inc-bot: Incident RW-INC-2026-418 opened by ashley (support). Severity: P2. Assigned: eng-infra, netops.

elaine-contoso: Ok — our security team confirmed they can add an exception. They asked for the IP ranges / hostnames to whitelist.

ashley (support): Provide them this minimal guidance: 1) Add TLS-inspection bypass for control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal (preserve SNI and do not terminate mTLS). 2) Allow outbound TCP 443 to Redwood control plane IPs: 34.198.12.145, 34.198.12.146, and 3) If IPs are ephemeral, allow DNS name based passthrough for control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal.

jin (eng-infra): Also ask them to allow TLS 1.2+ and ECDHE ciphers. If they must intercept, they must be configured in transparent proxy/pass-through mode and preserve client certificate forwarding (rare).

samir (netops): Quick repro steps for your security team:
1) From a host behind the appliance run `openssl s_client -connect control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal:443 -servername control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal -cert client.crt -key client.key`. This should succeed.
2) From the same host, force traffic through the appliance (or use a web proxy) and repeat — it will fail if interception is active.
3) If failure occurs, enable bypass for that FQDN and re-run the test.

elaine-contoso: Security added the exception to bypass TLS inspection for that FQDN and we just tested. The openssl command now completes successfully and our service reconnected. Thanks!

ashley (support): Great news. I'll update RW-INC-2026-418 with root cause = "Corporate TLS inspection appliance terminated mTLS and rewrote SNI, breaking client cert validation." Resolution: "Add TLS-inspection bypass / preserve SNI for control-plane.contoso.redwood.internal and allow outbound TCP 443 to Redwood control-planeIPs."

jin (eng-infra): I'll add a short KB note on the Private deployment docs about TLS inspection pitfalls and sample `openssl s_client` checks.

ashley (support): Closing thread after we log the KB and confirm remediation. :white_check_mark:
